title: hoa_fined_my_parkour_course
beats: My HOA fined me $50 a day for 'unauthorized structures' in my backyard, so I turned my entire yard into a Minecraft-style parkour course out of spite.
It started with one small fine for a birdhouse my nephew built.
Then the HOA president, a 61-year-old man named Gary who has never once minded his own business, started walking his dog past my fence just to find more violations.
Trellis? Fined. Garden gnome collection? Fined. Decorative gravel? Somehow also fined.
So I read the actual bylaws, all 40 pages, and found the loophole: temporary recreational equipment for personal use is exempt if removed within 24 hours.
I built jump blocks, floating platforms, and parkour towers out of pallets and installed them every single morning at 6 AM, then legally tore it all down every night before inspection.
Gary showed up daily with his little clipboard, fuming, unable to fine a structure that technically wasn't there anymore.
For three straight weeks I turned my yard into a live-action parkour map, and neighborhood kids started showing up to watch me speedrun my own backyard.
Gary tried to change the bylaw at the next meeting to ban 'temporary structures' entirely.
The vote failed 14 to 2, because apparently everyone else on the board thought a grown man rage-timing a toddler's obstacle course was the best entertainment the cul-de-sac had seen in years.
Send this to the one friend whose HOA has absolutely ruined their personality.
AITAH for turning malicious compliance into a full parkour career?
